question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-5t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{1+t})\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{1+{t}^{2}}\,i+(6t-5)\,j-\frac{1}{(1+t)^{2}}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute ${f}^{′}(1)$ we substitute $t=1$ into the expression for ${f}^{′}(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1) & =\frac{1}{1+(1)^{2}}\,i+(6(1)-5)\,j-\frac{1}{(1+(1))^{2}}\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,i+\,j-\frac{1}{4}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
